messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
I need layout and design assistance for an RFP response (proposal). The submission will have firm requirements for file size, page numbers, and similar items. Given how RFP schedules work, the turnaround will likely be last-minute. I believe the RFP may be released this month. 1) Have you supported this kind of proposal before? 2) If you have, how do you plan with clients for these timelines, especially when client edits may continue until the proposal is final?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

Yes, I routinely provide support for RFP responses that must meet strict compliance standards, including page limits, file size restrictions, formatting requirements, and compressed turnaround schedules. This has been central to my design work for the past 15+ years.

I use a process designed for tight timelines:
• As soon as the RFP is issued, I immediately create a compliant template and verify every technical requirement, including margins, fonts, file size, submission details, etc.
• I coordinate with your internal workplan and review calendar while allowing flexibility for edits as they come in
• I reserve the final 48–72 hours exclusively for redline reviews, late content additions, QA/QC, and optimization of the final PDF

I’ve handled this workflow many times and understand how to remain composed under pressure while delivering a polished, compliant submission by the deadline.

I’d be glad to schedule a call to talk through your specific RFP and the qualifications I can bring to your team.

Best regards,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
This is exactly what I was hoping to hear! Thank you, [FREELANCER_NAME_001].

I’ll follow up later tonight or tomorrow with some possible dates for a call.

Thank you again, and talk to you then!

messages.text: Great! Thank you!

messages.text: Thank you, [FREELANCER_NAME_001]! I feel the same. I just reviewed the existing proposal. Altogether, the document has 83 pages, counting all letters, forms, etc. Of those 83 pages, 55 pages include a graphic treatment. Could you share an estimated budget range for your project support? Please provide one budget that includes 1 simple infographic and 1 simple map, along with another budget that excludes both items. Thank you!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:

For custom proposal design of this kind, I generally estimate 1 to 1.5 hours per page. This accounts for the layout and graphic treatment of all 55 design-focused pages, as well as every meeting, revision, on-demand assistance during the final 48 hours before submission, delivery of the complete final document, and broader proposal support from start to finish.

Using that estimate, the two requested budget options are:
- Excluding the infographic and map: $3,800–$4,500
- Including 1 simple infographic and 1 simple map: $4,100–$4,800

I can work either hourly or for a fixed fee, whichever is the better fit for you. Please let me know whether these ranges are close to what you had in mind. I’m willing to make adjustments in response to your feedback.

Considering the RFQ and expected number of pages, I would charge $2,400 for this project. The fee covers:
- Proposal design and creative direction
- Layout and graphic treatment for the entire document
- Creation of a unified visual theme that aligns with both the RFQ and the client
- Addition of graphics, photos, tables, and any other needed visual components
- All meetings, revisions, and ongoing support, including on-demand assistance in the period leading up to submission
- Final production and delivery of the full proposal package

If this arrangement works for you, I’ll submit a proposed contract through Upwork. We can then schedule a brief kickoff call to coordinate the timeline, proposal strategy, and design direction.

messages.text: Unfortunately, that exceeds my budget and seems broader than the scope I need. Could we develop a more straightforward option? I’m envisioning a single formatting/layout pass on the final draft using GreenLatinos' existing brand colors and fonts, including one revision round and delivery as a print-ready PDF. More specifically, I believe I need 1) the full document laid out with graphic treatment and 2) tables, photos, the org chart, and graphics integrated into the final draft. I’m also assuming an RFP could potentially follow later, since the RFQ is typically the first step. What would you charge for this revised version?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I’m happy to tailor the scope to what you need. My fee would be $1,400 for a single formatting/layout pass on the final draft using GreenLatinos' existing brand colors and fonts, plus one round of revisions.

The fee would cover:
• Layout and graphic treatment for the complete document
• Incorporating tables, photos, the org chart, and other graphics into the final draft
• One revision round
• Delivery of a print-ready PDF along with a Canva design link

A few important notes:
• To stay within this timeline and budget, I’d prefer that all final content be provided together at once, including text, tables, photos, the org chart, and any additional supporting materials.
• I’ll need three business days to prepare the first draft, followed by two days for the revision.
• I’ll build the layout in Canva, allowing you or your team to handle any final content changes needed after the revision round.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Thank you for providing the $1400.00 estimate. That works for me.

A few items—

1) My subcontractors won’t deliver their content to me until EOD next Wednesday, so your available work time will be compressed. Could you manage a 48-hour turnaround after I send the finalized narrative content, followed by a 24-hour turnaround on your side for the final revisions?

2) For the branding, I’ve shifted the focus away from the client and to the bidder, which is me! I want the design to reflect my company’s identity, Agua Arc. I can provide a logo and colors.

3) Because this will be the first proposal I submit as a prime—and I launched my company less than a year ago and work solo—I’d like to use this proposal as a template going forward. Ideally, what you create would have modular, swappable sections so future proposals don’t need to be rebuilt from scratch. I’m specifically imagining a) a narrative structure that can accommodate different numbers of sections, such as 5 sections v 8 sections, b) a modular table design that can be resized for different budget formats, and c) a “prepared for \_\_\_ \[client name\]” credit line in place of client branding.

4) Regarding Canva, can I own the files without having a paid subscription? Would any other source files be included, or would everything exist solely in Canva?

Thank you!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Congratulations on the launch of Agua Arc! It’s exciting to contribute to your first proposal as a prime.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
1) That timing is workable for me. Just to verify the dates, I’d prepare the first draft on Thursday the 24th and Friday the 25th, with revisions taking place on Tuesday the 28th.

2) I’m glad to base the design on Agua Arc's identity rather than GreenLatinos. Please send your logo, colors, and any additional reference content I should use.

3) The modular template system you outlined would be a valuable long-term asset for your business, but it falls outside the quoted scope. Creating a system that can adapt to future proposals with different section counts and budget structures requires more design work and testing than a layout intended for a single use. I’d be happy to develop it, but I’d want to quote it separately to keep things fair for both of us. Would you prefer an add-on quote for the modular template now, or should we keep this first proposal straightforward and return to the template later as a separate project?

4) I’ll work exclusively with free Canva assets, so the file won’t contain any Pro-only elements. After it’s completed, I’ll give you full edit access. You’ll own the file and can independently reuse or modify it for future proposals, including replacing client information, content, and project details.

messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

I’ve attached the proposal’s first draft. The Canva link is here: [URL_006]

Please keep the following notes in mind during your review:

• **General design:** Because the document grew to nearly twice its anticipated length and the schedule was tight, I prioritized a cohesive design system instead of developing many distinct layouts. This should make revisions more manageable as well.

• **Graphics & photos:** I placed images in organic-shaped frames and incorporated several understated graphic elements that seemed appropriate for the overall theme without distracting from the content.

• **Section 6: Prioritization:** I didn’t find this section in the updated tables document, so I wasn’t certain whether it should remain in the proposal.

• **In-text bolding:** I wasn’t fully clear about which text was supposed to appear in bold. Some material in the Google Doc was highlighted while other text appeared in red, and once I began laying it out, I couldn’t determine which formatting was deliberate and which was editorial markup.

• **Links:** I checked all hyperlinks, and they seem to function correctly. However, it would be helpful to have a second reviewer test each one too.

• **Final review:** Given the very tight turnaround, I plan to take another pass tomorrow with fresh eyes to identify anything I might have overlooked. I still wanted to deliver this to you today.

I’m looking forward to your feedback. Hopefully the proposal is in a solid place, and after your review I can fine-tune anything you want changed.
